validation_notes: The variables, membership breakpoints, rule weights, and category thresholds are demonstration assumptions.
Qualified specialists in flood hazards, engineering geology, seismology, disaster-risk reduction, and land-use planning must review and validate this configuration before operational use.
Historical incidents and CLUP references are displayed as decision context; they are not numerical fuzzy inputs in this model version.
An unavailable required input produces an incomplete assessment. It is never converted to zero or interpreted as low vulnerability.
ULAP classification-to-index transformations below are transparent capstone assumptions and require validation by qualified MGB, PHIVOLCS, DRRM, geotechnical, and planning specialists.
Official ULAP codes and labels remain unchanged in the source result; the separate normalized index is used only by the Basafe fuzzy model.

inputs.name: Flood susceptibility
inputs.description: Normalized screening representation of the available flood classification at the selected point.

normalization.method: Exact code lookup from the verified live domain; the official label is preserved separately.
normalization.missing_value_policy: An absent feature, missing field, changed schema, or unknown code remains missing and makes the assessment incomplete.
normalization.validation_requirement: DEMONSTRATION TRANSFORMATION â€” the four model index values require review and approval by qualified domain experts before official planning use.

inputs.name: Liquefaction susceptibility
inputs.description: Normalized screening representation of the available liquefaction classification at the selected point.

normalization.source_domain: Live ArcGIS coded-value domain containing two distinct classification families
normalization.method: Exact code lookup configured independently for every official category; no ordinal sequence is inferred from the code numbers.

01.note: Broad legacy/general category; deliberately not treated as Low Potential.

normalization.missing_value_policy: An absent feature, missing field, changed schema, or unknown code remains missing and makes the assessment incomplete.
normalization.validation_requirement: DEMONSTRATION TRANSFORMATION â€” these non-equivalent source categories and all seven model index values require PHIVOLCS/domain-expert validation before official planning use.

inputs.name: Ground-shaking intensity
inputs.description: Normalized screening representation of the available ground-shaking classification at the selected point.

normalization.source_domain: PHIVOLCS Earthquake Intensity Scale (PEIS) coded-value domain
normalization.method: Exact PEIS code lookup from the verified PHIVOLCS domain. The ordinal PEIS I-X classes are transparently scaled to 10-100; the official Roman-numeral class remains separate.

00.note: Sentinel: point lies outside any mapped ground-shaking polygon. Treated as lowest intensity for screening purposes only.

normalization.missing_value_policy: A point outside all mapped ground-shaking polygons is assigned code 00 (normalized_value 0). A missing field or unknown code still blocks the assessment.
normalization.validation_requirement: DEMONSTRATION TRANSFORMATION — the PEIS-to-index scaling requires PHIVOLCS and domain-expert validation before official planning use.

rule_generation.coverage: All 27 combinations of the three ordinal hazard terms are generated at model load time.
rule_generation.monotonicity: Increasing any one antecedent term while holding the others constant never lowers the consequent term.

equal_weight_fallback.condition: Entropy weights cannot be calculated from a documented representative dataset and the assessment is explicitly labelled as using the equal-weight research baseline.

notes: Entropy weights must be calculated from a documented representative dataset and stored with the model version before operational scoring.
Rule weights remain separate confidence modifiers and must not be presented as indicator weights.

Very Low: Keep the individual source layers visible and verify site-specific conditions before making land-use or investment decisions.
A very-low relative screening result does not mean no hazard and must not be described as safe.
Low: Maintain current risk-reduction measures and verify site-specific conditions before committing land-use or capital decisions.
Keep hazard and incident records current; a low screening result does not mean no hazard.
Moderate: Include the location in more detailed planning review and compare the result with current official hazard maps.
Consider site inspection and appropriate professional advice before approving sensitive or high-occupancy uses.
High: Prioritize detailed site-specific hazard assessment and risk-reduction options before major planning or investment decisions.
Review applicable evacuation, drainage, structural, and land-use controls with qualified municipal and technical personnel.
Very High: Treat the location as a priority for detailed multi-hazard investigation and cautious land-use review.
Avoid using this screening result alone to approve development; obtain current official assessments and qualified technical advice.
Incomplete: Do not infer low vulnerability. Obtain the missing required hazard information and run the assessment again.
Use available incident and CLUP context only as supporting information, not as a substitute for missing hazard inputs.

disclaimer: This report is a preliminary multi-hazard screening output based on selected available data. It does not certify that a location is safe or unsafe and does not replace official hazard, planning, engineering, geological, geotechnical, or regulatory assessment.
